quote: A camera-reflex would have loved her, but there were only a few late-morning strollers and a boy sweeping leaves; the presence around her was not a crowd but a sheen—an expectation that some spectacle might arrive if one only waited long enough.
Tom had kept rooms above the shop for fifty years and could place a new arrival by the knock.

“Good morning,” he said to no one and everyone, sweeping the last grit off the door-mat. His voice was the mild, slightly ironic voice of someone who had watched generations of summer suits come and go.
